answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may submit jobs, then slash that stake when a randomly selected, independently verifiable task reveals fraud or duplicate control. This makes creating many aliases insufficient: each one needs separate capital at risk, and a successful attack can destroy the locked funds. For example, a comet-routing task at a jetty might be checked against public sensor records, while juniper labels help distinguish the benchmark cases. The defense raises the attacker’s cost; it does not prove every identity is unique.
